338579.title: Diameter bounds conjecture for cyclic shift components in patience sorting monoids
338579.review_depth: primary body read (Alg 2.1, Lemmas 3.3-3.8, Thm 3.7, Tables 1-2); exact computation
338579.disposition: Upper bound 2n-4 is source Lemma 3.4 (proved). The lower bound n-1 is proved in the source only for standard elements (Lemma 3.6). Found: source Lemma 3.8 is false at n=4 (evaluations (2,1,1,1), (3,1,1,1), etc. have diameter 3 > 2n-6 = 2), so it does not refute the lower bound. Sweep finds no violation of either bound.
338579.coverage: All evaluations with n=3,4,5 symbols and length<=9; n=6: 33 evaluations (length 6-9, <=4e5 words, time-capped); n=7: 8 evaluations. Minimum diameter: 2,3,4 (=n-1) for n=3,4,5; 6 for n=6; 8 for n=7. Tables 1-2 reproduced (one vertex count differs: (1,2,1,2,2) gives 495, source prints 711).
338579.remaining: Proof of the n-1 lower bound for non-standard elements (a statistic generalising cocharge that is rps-invariant and changes by <=1 per cyclic shift). Lemma 3.8 erratum is a source correction (zero credit).

338887.title: Conjecture on recurrent component cardinalities in sinkless rotor networks
338887.arxiv_title: Abelian networks IV. Dynamics of nonhalting networks
338887.journal_ref: Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 276 (2022), no. 1358, vii+89 pp
338887.review_depth: primary body read (Sec. 3.6 Ex. 3.11, Thm 7.4, Lemma 5.19, Thm 7.11, Sec. 8.3, Table 8.1), v1 and v2 checked; exact computation; complete ordinary proof
338887.disposition: Conjecture 8.3 proved for all n>=3, m>=1, with an explicit formula. Evaluate the weight generating function at a primitive e-th root, e | n. The domino transfer matrices give a period trace forced by rotation and degree to equal 2+q_e t^e; Cayley-Hamilton then gives rational coefficients depending only on e; Galois/Ramanujan sums finish. Independent of the source lemmas except the cycle-test bridge.
338887.coverage: Exact DP for 3<=n<=40, 1<=m<=3n (2451 (n,m) rows): conjecture true on every row; the closed formula matches every row; the trace identity is verified exactly in Q(zeta)[t] for e<=12.
338887.remaining: Lean: discharge recCount_add_m, orbit, recCount_mul_unit, W_primitive (plan in outputs/338887-lean-plan.md). Root ruling on the count-form endpoint versus full abelian-network semantics. Unread: AMS Memoir published version; citing literature.

339402.title: The approximation conjecture for the strong geodetic number of complete bipartite graphs
339402.arxiv_title: Strong geodetic problem on complete multipartite graphs
339402.review_depth: primary body read (eq.(1), Thm 2.1, Conj 2.4); Gledel-Iršič arXiv:1810.04004 Thm 2.4 body read
339402.disposition: e(m,n)<2 follows in a few lines from Gledel-Iršič (2018) Theorem 2.4. Case 4: sg = min{G(ceil x*-1), F(ceil x*)}, which lies in [k*, k*+2) because f and g are monotone. Case 3: sg=n and the intermediate value theorem gives a real root with k in [n, n+9/8]. Routine; low significance.
339402.coverage: All n<=110, n<=m<=C(n,2): max e = 1.787 (n=110); reproduces source data 1.094 (n=10), 1.774 (n=100); a real solution always exists.

339418.title: The odd-order obstruction conjecture for multi-part transitive n-partition orientations
339418.arxiv_title: Partitioning transitive tournaments into isomorphic digraphs
339418.review_depth: primary body read (Defs 1,2,4, Thm 3, Prop 3, Conjs 1-2)
339418.disposition: No counterexample. Exact reformulation: an order L on Z_n works iff every comparison sequence s_d(b)=[L(b)<L(b+d)] jumps only at one residue class mod k. Merging parts shows a counterexample for k gives one for every divisor k'>1 of k, so prime k>=5 is the regime the source never searched.
339418.remaining: Proof idea not completed: block-constancy forces equal rank sums per residue class and congruent local extrema. Larger cases need a better solver; SAT is forbidden in this lane.

340073.title: The strongly e-positive graph characterization conjecture
340073.arxiv_title: Classes of graphs with e-positive chromatic symmetric function
340073.review_depth: primary statement read (FHM arXiv:1808.03391 v1); 2026 literature read (arXiv:2607.21508 body)
340073.disposition: No counterexample. Exhaustive: every (claw,net)-free graph on <=11 vertices is e-positive (source verified <=9).
340073.coverage: All isomorphism classes of (claw,net)-free graphs on n<=11 vertices (by one-vertex extension; class is hereditary): n=10: 29551 classes (22386 connected); n=11: 195956 classes (158791 connected); all connected ones e-positive. Self-tests: claw, net, P4, C4 expansions; chromatic polynomial check; brute-force stable partition check.
340073.remaining: n=12 sweep (about 325M candidate extensions of connected 11-vertex graphs; several CPU-hours in pure Python). Matherne-Morales 2026 non-Schur-positive claw-free examples contain nets, so they are irrelevant.

340074.disposition: Same mathematical content as 340073 (contrapositive). Same exhaustive coverage through 11 vertices.

340151.title: Delannoy face-number conjecture for state polytopes of P(l,0,…,0)
340151.arxiv_title: State Polytopes Related to Two Classes of Combinatorial Neural Codes
340151.disposition: Needs universal Groebner bases/state polytopes of toric ideals (Macaulay2/CoCoA class), not available in the lane. The printed formula is garbled in pdftotext; the MathDB paraphrase C(n-1,k)C(2(n-1),n-1) is not the Delannoy count (with k diagonal steps the count is C(n-1,k)C(2(n-1)-k,n-1), the cyclohedron f-vector). Also, l versus n in the statement is ambiguous.
340151.remaining: Gröbner fan computation for small n; fidelity check of the printed formula from the TeX source.

340286.title: Polynomiality conjecture for Lecture Hall polynomials
340286.arxiv_title: The Lecture Hall Cone as a toric deformation
340286.review_depth: primary body read (Def 3.1, Prop 3.3, Conj 3.4; l_1..l_8 list)
340286.disposition: No counterexample. Exact specialise-and-interpolate test (a negative power after integer specialisation would certify non-polynomiality) finds none.
340286.coverage: i<=22 with each of y_1..y_22 free; i<=40 with y_j free for j in {1,2,3,5,8,13,20,30,39,40}; other variables fixed random integers in [2,7] (one specialisation per run, so this is not a proof of polynomiality). Source verified i<=12.
340286.remaining: A proof would need polynomiality in the Desnanot-Jacobi/octahedron recurrence on Toeplitz minors with monomial boundary data.
